name: Tasmania Road Safety Advisory Council (RSAC)
policy_chain: Tasmania’s advisory council contributed to Towards Zero 2017–2026 and action-plan monitoring; the state government released the strategy and ministerial authorities retain funding decisions.
evidence_boundary: A state advisory and implementation-monitoring mechanism, not a national government council. Its official role must not be conflated with the government’s approval powers.
transferable_lesson: Councils need explicit ministerial approval routes and agency delivery responsibilities.

name: Conselho Nacional de Trânsito (CONTRAN)
policy_chain: CONTRAN formally approved PNATRANS instruments through council resolutions; the national transport secretariat and other agencies deliver the activities.
evidence_boundary: An adopting council resolution establishes policy authority, not direct execution by every council member. Subsequent resolutions can supersede older rules.
transferable_lesson: Keep resolution histories and distinguish approval from programme delivery.

name: National Road Safety Council (MKKJR)
policy_chain: The National Road Safety Council developed Road Safety Action 2030, organized through enforcement, technical/infrastructure, research and media/outreach action groups.
evidence_boundary: Subgroups are functional components of a council, not necessarily separate statutory agencies or formal seats.
transferable_lesson: Assign the work of each action group to a named organization with monitoring responsibilities.

name: State-Public Consultative Commission on Road Traffic Safety Problems
policy_chain: The national commission contributes to national strategy and operational plans; the Council of Ministers formally adopts national programmes.
evidence_boundary: Historical and revised ministry rosters must be distinguished. The December 2025 strategy update and 2026 plan need clear adoption records.
transferable_lesson: Separate commission endorsement, Cabinet adoption, and line-ministry execution.

name: National Road Safety Committee (NRSC)
policy_chain: The National Road Safety Committee and its Secretariat coordinated the 2021–2030 plan with sectoral ministries and provincial/other participants.
evidence_boundary: A cross-sector drafting process does not prove permanent formal membership or specific responsibilities for every consulted organization.
transferable_lesson: Document the formal ministerial roster separately from temporary contributors.

name: Canadian Council of Motor Transport Administrators (CCMTA)
policy_chain: The Canadian Council of Motor Transport Administrators coordinates the intergovernmental road safety strategy and technical work; provinces and territories retain regulatory and delivery authority.
evidence_boundary: The newer 2035+ strategy supersedes older RSS 2025-only descriptions, and ministerial approval differs from CCMTA technical custodianship.
transferable_lesson: Intergovernmental coordination is not equal to legal authority over subnational implementation.

name: Comisión Nacional de Seguridad de Tránsito (CONASET)
policy_chain: CONASET contributed technically to the 2017 policy and 2021–2030 strategy, with a newer 2026 edition reflecting expanded proposals.
evidence_boundary: Proposed actions, consultation, approval, and completed sectoral interventions must remain separate evidence categories.
transferable_lesson: Link each Safe System action to a responsible government unit and dated source.

name: Consejo de Seguridad Vial (COSEVI)
policy_chain: COSEVI produced an institutional strategic plan and annual operating plans with budget and programme elements.
evidence_boundary: An institutional council strategy does not, by itself, represent the entire country’s interministerial national road safety strategy.
transferable_lesson: Keep institutional planning and national policy instruments separately classified.

name: National road safety plan implementation working group (MUP)
policy_chain: The national 2021–2030 plan was adopted by government, with an Interior Minister-appointed working group responsible for implementation coordination and annual evaluation.
evidence_boundary: The reviewed audit maps the plan’s action table to the 85-cell framework; the existence of assigned activities does not demonstrate delivery or fatality reductions.
transferable_lesson: Require source-specific action owners, budgets, deadlines and monitoring.

name: Road Safety Council and seven interdepartmental committees
policy_chain: The Road Safety Council and seven interdepartmental committees contributed to the 2021–2030 strategy and a structured portfolio of proposed measures.
evidence_boundary: Detailed committee structures support planned-role coding but not evidence of completed measures or accountable financing.
transferable_lesson: Link a seven-committee model to agency-level action tracking and outcome evaluation.

name: Government Council for Road Traffic Safety / BESIP
policy_chain: BESIP coordination structures participated in the national strategy, while government authorities approved the council-endorsed 2025–2026 action plan.
evidence_boundary: The earlier 11-domain/6-intervention totals are provisional. The full action plan needs item-by-item reassessment.
transferable_lesson: Trace endorsement, government approval and programme ownership independently.

name: Government Traffic Commission (Liikluskomisjon)
policy_chain: The Traffic Commission endorsed the 2026–2035 road safety programme and formally approved its 2026–2029 implementation plan in February 2026; government approved the strategy in December 2025.
evidence_boundary: Strategy endorsement, Government adoption, and Commission adoption of the implementation plan are different recorded actions.
transferable_lesson: Use dated approval instruments and the rolling programme to establish responsibility.

name: Comité interministériel de la sécurité routière (CISR)
policy_chain: The Prime Minister-chaired Interministerial Road Safety Committee adopted 38 decisions in July 2023, with the road safety delegation organizing follow-up.
evidence_boundary: The wider advisory council CNSR must not be treated as the same institution, and 38 decisions do not imply implementation.
transferable_lesson: Distinguish the PM-led decision forum, technical secretariat and delivery organizations.

name: Central Traffic Safety Measures Council (中央交通安全対策会議)
policy_chain: The Prime Minister-chaired Central Traffic Safety Measures Council formally adopted the 12th Basic Traffic Safety Plan in March 2026.
evidence_boundary: The Council, Cabinet Office coordination and separate Traffic Measures Headquarters are distinct from executing ministries and local bodies.
transferable_lesson: Sustain five-year plans with formal government-wide responsibilities and periodic evaluation.

name: Higher Council for Traffic Safety (المجلس الأعلى للسلامة المرورية)
policy_chain: The statutory Higher Council for Traffic Safety directly adopted the executive plan for the 2024–2028 national strategy in July 2025.
evidence_boundary: Document access limitations mean action assignments and implementation outcomes must not be inferred solely from the approval announcement.
transferable_lesson: Record both statutory membership and full executive action-plan access before assigning final roles.

name: Road Traffic Safety Council (Ceļu satiksmes drošības padome)
policy_chain: The Transport Minister-led Road Traffic Safety Council coordinates policy; ministry drafted the 2021–2027 plan and Cabinet adopted it. In 2026 the Council allocated support to road safety projects.
evidence_boundary: Project allocation is not verified spending or impact, and the council’s 2026 statutory membership differs from earlier rosters.
transferable_lesson: Require legal rosters and post-award monitoring to accompany funding decisions.

name: Group for Vision Zero Cooperation (GNS)
policy_chain: The GNS Vision Zero cooperation forum supports cross-agency coordination and road safety target development.
evidence_boundary: Sweden’s broad national delivery network must not be counted as the formal membership or intervention portfolio of GNS itself.
transferable_lesson: Define the exact unit of analysis before comparing coordination bodies.

name: Road Traffic Safety Strategy Coordination Board
policy_chain: The national coordination board works through the 2024–2027 Road Traffic Safety Action Plan and government technical groups, including disaster-response representation.
evidence_boundary: Formal membership is relatively well documented but intervention responsibility coding remains provisional; preserve AFAD-specific evidence boundaries.
transferable_lesson: Count disaster-management functions only when formally documented, not inferred.

name: Parliamentary Forum on Road Safety (PAFROS)
policy_chain: The Parliamentary Forum on Road Safety contributes to legislative advocacy and related road safety action planning.
evidence_boundary: A parliamentary forum does not hold the executive authority of the ministry-led national implementation system.
transferable_lesson: Separate legislative advocacy from Cabinet-level strategy oversight and agency delivery.

name: Strategic Road Safety Forum
policy_chain: The Strategic Road Safety Forum contributed to Northern Ireland’s Road Safety Strategy to 2030 and subsequent action planning.
evidence_boundary: Forum representation and January 2026 implementation annex require distinction from full department execution and victim-safety outcomes.
transferable_lesson: Recognize devolved regional governance as distinct from UK-wide policy.

name: Governor’s Traffic Safety Committee (GTSC)
policy_chain: The Governor’s Traffic Safety Committee prepares and administers a multiyear Highway Safety Plan, including enforcement and grant programmes.
evidence_boundary: The statewide grant programme and the council’s planning responsibilities cannot be attributed to a national council.
transferable_lesson: Connect a committee’s grant allocations to a dated multiyear plan and delivery reports.

name: Washington Traffic Safety Commission (WTSC)
policy_chain: The Washington Traffic Safety Commission formally adopted Target Zero commissioner actions and contributed to statewide and tribal/local partnership plans.
evidence_boundary: Commission approval of its own action plan differs from co-authorship of a broader road safety strategy.
transferable_lesson: Separately record direct approval and cross-agency co-development.

name: Sistema Nacional de Movilidad y Seguridad Vial (SINAMOV)
policy_chain: SINAMOV, created under the 2022 General Law on Mobility and Road Safety, approved ENAMOV 2023–2042 on June 22, 2023; SEDATU published it October 10, 2023. Its amended operating rules were published in February 2026.
evidence_boundary: The one intergovernmental system spans national/state/municipal participation channels. Its initial 7/17 and 5/72 legacy figures are superseded and require complete reassessment.
transferable_lesson: Anchor each council governance obligation and Safe System measure to the statute or ENAMOV provision.

name: Krajowa Rada Bezpieczeństwa Ruchu Drogowego (KRBRD)
policy_chain: KRBRD adopted the 2021–2030 national programme and successive 2022–2023, 2024–2025 and 2026–2027 implementation programmes through council resolutions. Its Secretariat organizes reporting, while ministries and road authorities execute measures.
evidence_boundary: The September 11, 2026 programme includes 31 planned actions and identifies leaders, funding and indicators, but adoption is not evidence of completed delivery.
transferable_lesson: Adopt short-cycle implementation programmes with named leaders, funded tasks and annual reporting.

name: National Traffic Safety Committee (NTSC)
policy_chain: The National Traffic Safety Committee is established through Cabinet legal instruments and coordinates the second Road Safety Strategy 2025–2030, with five Safe System pillars, nine implementation programmes and a planned 2028 midterm review.
evidence_boundary: The strategy’s precise approval resolution and complete project-level budgets are not independently established; the historical first strategy was 2013–2022.
transferable_lesson: Give cross-sector programmes a formal committee, Secretariat, project register and midterm review.

name: Consiliul Interministerial pentru Siguranță Rutieră (CISR)
policy_chain: CISR is a government consultative body with a technical delegation; the Romanian Government formally adopted the 2022–2030 strategy under Decision 682/2022. Decision 144/2023 replaced the action-plan annexes.
evidence_boundary: The 2023 annexes specify actions, owners, dates and financing sources, but are not a second national strategy or evidence of implementation.
transferable_lesson: Separate technical council drafting, Cabinet approval, and agency-level action tracking.

name: Telo za koordinaciju poslova bezbednosti saobraćaja na putevima
policy_chain: Serbia’s Article 8 coordination body initiated strategy development; the Road Traffic Safety Agency organized drafting with 32 organizations. The Government adopted the 2023–2030 strategy and 2023–2025 action plan on September 28, 2023.
evidence_boundary: Eight formal statutory positions are not interchangeable with 32 drafting organizations. A successor 2026–2028 action plan is documented in preparation, not verified as adopted.
transferable_lesson: Formalize the chain from ministerial council to technical agency, stakeholders, Government adoption and accountable delivery.
